about: The AI's numbers (design section 7 and the appendix's AI skill note). Pilot profiles are FS2's AI classes: four skill knobs per difficulty level (accuracy 0..1; evasion, courage, patience 0..100), copied from FS2's ai.tbl where named in 'fs2' ('ai.tbl <class> <field>') or ours with a 'source'. The difficulty tables are the per-skill-level arrays FS2's own code keeps (aicode.cpp, ship.cpp). How each knob is used is in Scripts/AI/README.md.

turnTimeScale.unit: x turn time, Earth's side only
turnTimeScale.fs2: aicode.cpp Turn_time_skill_level_scale (applied to ships not on the player's team)

inRangeTime.unit: s added to the time a pilot needs on a target before its aim settles

retargetSeconds.unit: s, longest wait before a pilot looks for a better target (half of it at shortest)
retargetSeconds.source: FS2 aicode.cpp ai_frame: the next enemy re-choice comes 3 x (5 - skill level) x 0.5..1 s later

cmeasureChance.unit: chance per missile, scaled by evasion

hostileFireDelay.unit: x every weapon's fire wait, Earth's AI ships and turrets

friendlyFireDelay.unit: x every weapon's fire wait, our side's AI ships and turrets

maxPlayerAttackers.unit: Earth fighters on the player at once

maxPlayerHomers.unit: missiles homing on the player at once

predictDelay.unit: s an Earth pilot's picture of its target is out of date (it aims from that picture)
predictDelay.fs2: aicode.cpp Skill_level_delay (ai_set_positions keeps the enemy's position this long before refreshing it)

playerDamageScale.unit: x weapon damage to the player's ship

playerPartDamageScale.unit: x damage to the player's ship's parts, on top

aimErrorMetres.unit: m of aim error at accuracy 0 and aiming error 1
aimErrorMetres.source: ours, from FS2's set_predicted_enemy_pos ((1 - accuracy) x 4 x a random vector, up to 5x when the target has only just come into range); in metres here, calibrated with the arena

turretAimError.unit: x range (m) per (1 - accuracy) x aiming error
turretAimError.source: ours: turret bolts scatter more the further the target is, so a weaving fighter at range is safe and a slow one close in is not

flakSpreadMetres.source: ours: FS2 jitters flak aim so bursts bracket the target; this is the radius for a gunner of accuracy 0.5, smaller for better gunners

flakLeadSeconds.source: ours: flak is aimed up to this far along the target's path past the intercept, so the bursts open in front of it (design section 7: flak bursts in the player's path)

peelHullNoCourage.source: ours: a pilot with no courage (and not fearless) pulls out of the fight at half hull

peelHullFullCourage.source: ours: a pilot with full courage stays in until 15% hull (design section 7: courage is how long a pilot stays in a fight when hurt)

peelMaxSeconds.source: ours: a pilot that has pulled out comes back after this long at most (the diaspora's ships mend slowly while out of the fight)

patienceHoldSeconds.source: ours: design section 7, patience is how long a pilot holds a firing line before shooting (FS2 dogfight firing windows are short: longer holds lose more shots than they save)

patienceConeBlend.source: ours: a patient pilot narrows FS2's firing cone (aicode.cpp: dot > 0.90 + accuracy/10 - radius/distance) towards the target's own size by this much at patience 100

tailRange.source: ours: 'on the tail' for the measurements: within this range

tailNoseDegrees.source: ours: 'on the tail': the target is within this angle of the chaser's nose

tailAspectDegrees.source: ours: 'on the tail': the chaser is within this angle of the target's tail

avoidMargin.source: ours: fighters keep this far (plus their own size) off a capital hull's boxes

avoidLookAheadMin.source: ours: how far ahead a fighter checks its path against capital hulls, at low speed

avoidLookAheadMax.source: ours: and at high speed (FS2 predicts collisions up to 4 s ahead in ai_chase)

gunRangeFraction.source: ours: pilots open fire when the bolt would arrive within this share of its life

sensorRange.source: ours: how far a pilot looks for targets

flakEnvelope.source: ours: an enemy capital ship's guns reach about this far (flak 1,125 m, turret lasers 1,375 m); a pilot who fears for itself does not chase a fighter into it unless ordered to (fearless drones do)

drone.about: Earth's drone fighters, the bulk of their waves: Captain-class aim, Lieutenant-class evasion and patience, and no fear (design section 7: courage zero, no breaking off when hurt).

courage.source: design section 7: Earth's drones have FS2's courage at zero (they are fearless: courage has nothing to act on)

drone_heavy.about: Earth's heavier drones, escorts for bombers: Captain-class throughout, fearless.

drone_bomber.about: Earth's bomber drones: they press their torpedo runs and hardly jink.

evasion.source: ours: a bomber on its run holds its line

ascended_ace.about: One of Earth's ascended aces, for later (design section 7): General-class in every knob, and on every difficulty it turns and fires at its ship's full rate (FS2's easy-level handicaps do not apply) and never breaks off for fear.

wingman.about: The player's wingmen, diaspora pilots: Major-class. They pull out when badly hurt, mend, and come back.

autopilot.about: Flies the player's own ship in soaks and captures (never in play): Colonel-class (an invulnerable ship never pulls out).

earth_turret.about: Earth's capital-ship gunners (turrets use accuracy only).

diaspora_turret.about: Our capital ships' gunners (turrets use accuracy only).
